title: GST Returns, Payment and Electronic Ledgers

content.overview: A registered person files the returns the Act prescribes and pays tax into the electronic cash or credit ledger. Output tax, input credit and cash payments are recorded in the electronic ledgers. A return is the statement. The ledger is the payment record. Filing without payment does not discharge tax. Payment without a return does not complete compliance.
content.glance: GST Returns, Payment and Electronic Ledgers. Complete Tax treatise with statutory deconstruction, examples, verified authorities, forum analysis and chamber drafting.
content.study: Identify the return, the period, the ledgers used and whether tax was paid. Do not treat a ledger balance as a return.

cases.name: Govind Saran Ganga Saran v. Commissioner of Sales Tax
cases.facts: The Court examined the components of a valid charging provision.
cases.issue: What must a tax levy clearly identify to be valid?
cases.ratioDecidendi: A valid levy ordinarily identifies the taxable event, person liable, rate and measure or value of the tax.
cases.holding: The Court treated these components as essential to a charging scheme.
cases.relevance: Use for charge, levy and statutory certainty.

cases.name: Union of India v. Azadi Bachao Andolan
cases.facts: The Court considered treaty benefits, circulars and tax avoidance arguments.
cases.issue: How should a valid tax treaty and administrative circular operate?
cases.ratioDecidendi: A treaty and valid administrative practice must be respected unless displaced by law; legitimate tax planning is not automatically evasion.
cases.holding: The Court upheld the challenged treaty approach in the circumstances.
cases.relevance: Use for statutory interpretation, treaties and tax planning.

cases.name: Union of India v. Mohit Minerals Pvt. Ltd.
cases.facts: The case concerned GST levy and the legal effect of a Council recommendation.
cases.issue: What is the constitutional and statutory force of GST Council recommendations?
cases.ratioDecidendi: GST Council recommendations have persuasive value within the constitutional design but are not automatically binding as primary legislation without statutory implementation.
cases.holding: The Court interpreted the federal GST framework accordingly.
cases.relevance: Use for GST levy, delegated action and constitutional federalism.

enhancement.definition: A registered person files the returns the Act prescribes and pays tax into the electronic cash or credit ledger. Output tax, input credit and cash payments are recorded in the electronic ledgers. A return is the statement. The ledger is the payment record.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Filing without payment does not discharge tax. Payment without a return does not complete compliance.
essentialIngredients: Tax paid by the due date
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 37 is outward supplies. Section 38 is inward supplies. Section 39 is the periodic return and tax payment. Section 49 operates the electronic cash ledger, credit ledger and liability ledger. Interest on late payment is a separate demand consequence. The form numbers and due dates are rules and are not frozen here.
examples: A dealer declares outward supplies, sets off eligible credit, and pays the balance in cash.
Both the return and the ledger entry are required.
A credit balance cannot pay a liability the Act does not allow to be set off.
enhancement.problemApplication: Identify the return, the period, the ledgers used and whether tax was paid. Do not treat a ledger balance as a return.
enhancement.caseLawNotes: No new case citation or ratio was added. Rates and notifications are not frozen in this note.
